correctness.rationale: Smoothness and genus three follow from the stated gradient; on Y=0 the sole point is [0:0:1]. Independently computed the exact counts for all six admissible η using F₃[t] mod t²+1, t⁴+2t+2 and t⁶+2t+2, checking irreducibility and summing the multiplicities of z³+z at −η−x⁴. Every η gave (1,109,892). The corresponding power sums are (9,−27,−162); Newton's identities and the genus-three functional equation give (1−3T+9T²)³. There is also a direct all-η check: take b³+b=η, so b⁹=b+η³−η and b^(9³)=b. The substitution Z→Z+bY identifies the equation with the Hermitian quartic over F_{9³}. That Hermitian quartic has 28 F₉-points (nine affine x choices and three z choices per x, plus infinity), so its six F₉ eigenvalues are −3; over F_{9³} the eigenvalues are −27. The F₉ eigenvalues of C therefore lie in {−3,3e^(±iπ/3)}. The unique F₉ point makes the trace 9; conjugacy and degree six force the conjugate pair to have multiplicity three each, with no −3. Frobenius semisimplicity and the faithful Tate-module action give f(π)=0 for f(U)=U²−3U+9. On J(F₉), π=1 so f(1)=7 annihilates the group. Its order is L(1)=343, proving the displayed rank and exponent, without any inference from order alone. The eigenvalues give the cosine count formula. An elliptic class with trace 3 exists (e.g. y²=x³−x+1 over F₉ has seven points), so Tate gives the isogeny statement.
